newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs lose gains, new 2000 OLO thinly traded.
newsitem.headline: OLOs lose gains, new 2000 OLO thinly traded.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds initially continued Tuesday's corrective rally in early Wednesday trade, but quickly gave up gains as bearish sentiment took over again.
Many dealers said Tuesday's rise had been a short-covering spike and that bearish sentiment should take the market lower in the coming days and weeks.

The U.S. markets are expected to call the tune with 106 seen as key support on T-bond futures. The contract currently stands at 107*19 after having touched 106*12 on Friday. "Any sign of inflation will knock markets out again," one dealer said.
U.S. March housing starts are due at 1230 GMT (1430 Belgian time), capacity utilisation and industrial production data at 1315 GMT (1515 Belgian time).
Housing starts are seen at 1.5 million, industrial production at 0.6 percent, capacity utilisation at 83.6 percent.
Dealers said that the moribund mood on the OLO market was exemplified by the lack of trade in the new 4 percent, January 2000 OLO on the grey market.
"Usually, there is busy trade in a new issue as soon as it is announced. Now I hardly see any quotes," one Luxembourg dealer said.

The new OLO, which will be auctioned for the first time next Monday, was issued at banks' request. It will provide them with a new instrument for coverage of bank savings certificates and other liabilities in that maturity.
